sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker enteric valve architecture (EVA) is of the finitimus type, morphologically slightly closer to I. finitimus than to I. planifrons. The soldier is likewise slightly closer to I. finitimus than to I. planifrons, whereas the alate is clearly closer to I. planifrons. Specimens at present assigned to this species were first considered close to I. planifrons; besides the morphological confusion, their localities also lie outside the range of I. planifrons. This is a cryptic species reliably separated only by molecular means, so some specimens that could not be sequenced and were previously identified as I. finitimus may in fact belong here. As to ecology and distribution, it is at present known only from the Congo forest south of Kisangani, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule well sclerotized and dark (C6–C7); frontal gland pore concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus concolorous with the head capsule; antennae C5–C6, without difference between proximal and apical segments. Pronotum C6–C7, concolorous with the head capsule; meso- and metanotum C6–C7, concolorous with the pronotum; legs C3–C4; abdominal tergites C6–C7; sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C3–C4), darker at the sides (C4–C6), the posterior sternites (C4–C6) darker than the anterior ones. Head capsule with conspicuous setae scattered, mainly near the compound eyes, and with denser, shorter fine hairs all over; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip, especially distally (visible above 50×). Pronotum setae mainly on the margins, the middle with many short hairs; meso- and metanotum with fine pale hairs arranged along the median band (visible at 20×), the metanotum with or without 2 larger setae. Legs hairy, the fore coxa with 10–15 stronger setae on the ridge and 2 ventrally; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, the tibiae with 10–30 stronger setae. Abdominal tergites with setae of mixed sizes; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, together with many long and small setae directed posteriorly. Compound eyes nearly circular; frontal gland pore a small circular to elongate mark; ocelli nearly circular to oval, separated from the compound eye by about 0.8–0.9 times the small ocellar diameter. Labrum domed. Left mandible apical tooth always longer and more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 3 marginal teeth, the second expressed only as a slight undulation of the tooth margin between the first and third; the proximal premolar hidden by the molar prominence in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth longer and more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp-tipped, the second smaller and blunt; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Measurements: compound eye major diameter 0.41–0.45 mm, head width including compound eyes 1.52–1.60 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.21–0.22 mm, ocellus major diameter 0.18–0.20 mm, postclypeus width 0.70–0.79 mm, pronotum width 1.45–1.49 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule C4–C6; in one of the two specimens the head capsule shows a strong gradient from a darker frons to a paler posterior (e.g. C6→C4), so that it may look bicoloured; gulamentum, antennae and labrum concolorous with the head capsule; mandibles dark (C7–C8), the base generally abruptly two shades paler and generally concolorous with the frons; thorax and tergites C4, legs paler (C2–C3); abdomen grey from the gut contents, the tergites with a pale yellow tinge. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of hairs surrounds and covers the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum always with 5–6 large setae on each lateral lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with setae mainly on the margins. Fore coxa with 1–2 spines on the ridge and none ventrally; trochanter with several long setae and 4–5 spines in a row; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with a row of 7–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with the large setae only on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Soldier medium-sized within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides usually nearly parallel, slightly narrowing in the posterior 1/3–1/4, distinctly converging from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases; the upper margin distinctly concave; frons flat, without a swelling. Gulamentum narrowing in the posterior half in ventral view, the anterior half ear-like at the sides. Antennae 15-segmented. Labrum deeply forked, wider than long, the sides harp-shaped; the lobes angular, their tips semitransparent to white; the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, regularly curved; the inner margin smooth, each mandible with 1 distinct but very small marginal tooth near the molar area; mandibles distinctly shorter than the head; the surface of both smooth and shining. Pronotum saddle-shaped, distinctly narrower than the head, the anterior margin with a shallow notch, the posterior margin entire; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion 14%–18% longer than the even ones, the crest almost undeveloped, the crest marking the place where the setae abruptly become very dense; secondary cushions (SC) broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum small, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, lobed (3 lobules). Measurements: head dorsal concavity sagitta 0.02–0.06 mm, head length 2.97–3.30 mm, head width 2.00–2.20 mm, left mandible ventral length 2.33–2.38 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C2–C3); proximal antennal segments pale (C2), the apical segment two shades darker (C4); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); thoracic tergites with scattered setae. Fore coxa ridged, with 1 fine seta, 5 spines on the ridge and 2 ventrally; fore trochanter with 6–7 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, and with a row of spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Workers medium-sized on average within the genus, with much overlap with several species. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14.5 segmented. Labrum domed. Left mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp-tipped when fresh; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt even when fresh, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin), the third with a blunt tip; the proximal premolar hidden by the molar prominence; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 72% of the head width; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions arranged in the finitimus type with trigonal symmetry: the downstream part of the odd cushion is broad, its bulbous inflation bearing very dense shorter setae; supporting setae numerous, 25–27 on each side of the odd cushion; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum small, visible in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, with short lobes (3–4 lobules). Measurements: maximum head width 1.16–1.24 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.17–0.20 mm, left mandible functional length 0.55–0.62 mm, mean length of primary cushions 1–6 0.60–0.65 mm, mean width 0.07–0.08 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.48–0.56 mm, mean width 0.23–0.29 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 7.20–8.81.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; measurements from Table 15 and the text of the original; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
